title: Remark
body_md:
We follow \cites{bossmannBogoliubovDynamics2021,mitrouskasBogoliubovCorrectionsTrace2019,lewinFluctuationsHartreeStates2015,bossmannHigherOrderCorrections2020,namBogoliubovCorrectionMeanfield2017} for the normalization of the Hartree equation \eqref{eqn: hartree equation} using the coefficient \( \mu_{\varphi(t)} \) given in \eqref{eqn: mu in hartree equation}.
    The convenience of this coefficient will be clarified later in Section \ref{section: equations of motion - study of RHS}.

label: remark: scope and applicability of this work
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark: scope and applicability of this work}
    We do not claim that for small or moderate values of \( N \), the method introduced in this work can be as accurate as other methods, e.g. MCTDHB.
    Its interest lies in the large \( N \) limit, where other methods fail in practice.
    The method introduced in this work has to be understood as a first-order approximation, where the zero-th order term is the Hartree product state \( \varphi^{\otimes N} \): both methods can be applied in practice to any number of bosons, and they assume a non-physical (almost) complete Bose--Einstein condensation.
    Our method outperforms the Hartree method because it can additionally capture pair-interactions.

label: lemma: when does braket varphiN-m-p otimes chip vs A varphiN-j otimes chiq vanishes depending on p q s m
title: Lemma
head: environment
labels: lemma: when does braket varphiN-m-p otimes chip vs A varphiN-j otimes chiq vanishes depending on p q s m

title: Proof
body_md:
We start with a simple observation: the braket over \( N-m \) variables vanishes as soon as the braket over one of the variables is of the form \( \left\langle \begin{gathered} \varphi(y) \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} \chi_{2p}(y, \cdot) \end{gathered} \right\rangle \) or \( \left\langle \begin{gathered} \varphi(y) \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} \chi_{2q}(y, \cdot) \end{gathered} \right\rangle \), since those one-dimensional brakets vanish by \eqref{eqn: bogoliubov orthogonality relation}.
    Such brakets necessarily occur in the following situations:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item one of the functions \( \varphi \) on the left is paired with a marginal of \( \chi_{2q} \) on the right.
        It means we couldn't pair all functions \( \varphi \) from the left argument of the braket to those on the right argument or to marginals of \( \chi_{2q} \) upon which \( A \) is acting.
        This situation occurs when \( N-m-2p > N-2q+2 \iff 2q > 2p+m+2 \).

        \item one of the marginals of \( \chi_{2p} \) from the left argument of the braket is paired with a function \( \varphi \) from the right argument.
        It means we couldn't pair all marginals of \( \chi_{2p} \) on the left to marginals of \( \chi_{2q} \) on the right or to functions \( \varphi \) on which the operator acts.
        This situation occurs when \( 2p > 2q+2 \).
        
        \item a function \( \varphi \) from the right argument on the braket is paired with a marginal of \( \chi_{2p} \) from the left argument.
        It means we couldn't pair all functions \( \varphi \) from the right to those from the left argument or to marginals of \( \chi_{2p} \) where \( A \) is acting, or to put them outside the braket.
        This situation occurs when \( N-2q > N-m-2p + m + 2 \iff 2p > 2q+2 \).

        \item one of the marginals of \( \chi_{2q} \) from the right argument of the braket is paired with a function \( \varphi \) from the left argument. It means we couldn't pair all marginals of \( \chi_{2q} \) on the right to marginals of \( \chi_{2p} \) on the left or to functions \( \varphi \) on which the operator acts, or to put them outside the braket.
        This situation occurs when \( 2q > 2p+m+2 \).
    \end{enumerate}
    When any of these conditions is met, the braket vanishes by \eqref{eqn: bogoliubov orthogonality relation}.

label: lemma: symmetric tensor product rewritten with only unique permutations
title: Lemma
head: environment
labels: lemma: symmetric tensor product rewritten with only unique permutations
eqn: symmetric tensor product rewritten with only unique permutations

title: Proof
body_md:
We have
    \begin{equation*}
        (f\otimes_s g)(x)
        = \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}_{i}^{i+j}} \sum_{\sigma\in S_{i+j}} f(x_{\sigma(\left[1:i\right])}) g(x_{\sigma(\left[i+1:i+j\right])}) 
        = \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}_{i}^{i+j}} \sum_{\sigma_1 \in S^{j}_{i+j}} \sum_{\sigma_2 \in S_{i+j\setminus \sigma_1}} f(x_{\sigma_2}) g(x_{\sigma_1}),
    \end{equation*}
     
    where we have decomposed \( \sigma\in S_{i+j} \) as \( \sigma = (\sigma_2, \sigma_1) \), with \( \sigma_1 \in S_{i+j}^j \) and \( \sigma_2 \in S_{i+j\setminus \sigma_1} \).
    By symmetry of the function \( f \) we have \( f(x_{\sigma_2}) = f(x\setminus x_{\sigma_1}) \), hence
    \begin{equation*}
        (f\otimes_s g)(x)
        = \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}_{i}^{i+j}} \sum_{\sigma_1 \in S^{j}_{i+j}} \sum_{\sigma_2 \in S_{i+j\setminus \sigma_1}} f(x \setminus x_{\sigma_1}) g(x_{\sigma_1})
        = \frac{i!}{\mathsf{K}_{i}^{i+j}} \sum_{\sigma_1 \in S^{j}_{i+j}} f(x \setminus x_{\sigma_1}) g(x_{\sigma_1}).
    \end{equation*}
     
    By symmetry of the function \( g \) we have \( g(x_{\sigma_1}) = g(x_{\tau}) \) for all \( \tau \in S_{\sigma_1} \).
    Moreover, for each \( \sigma_1 \in S^j_{i+j} \), there is a unique permutation \( \tau \) such that \( \tau \) is sorted according to the given total ordering and \( \tau(\left[1:j\right]) =_s \sigma(\left[1:j\right]) \).
    Iterating over all \( \sigma_1 \in S^j_{i+j} \) is equivalent to iterating over all sorted permutations \( \tau \), and for each \( \tau \), over all its permutations.
    Thus,
    \begin{equation*}
        (f\otimes_s g)(x)
        = \frac{i!}{\mathsf{K}_{i}^{i+j}} \sum_{\substack{\tau\in S^j_{i+j}\\\tau\,\mathrm{sorted}}} \sum_{\mu \in S_\tau} f(x \setminus x_{\tau}) g(x_{\tau})
        = \frac{i!j!}{\mathsf{K}_{i}^{i+j}} \sum_{\substack{\tau\in S^j_{i+j}\\\tau\,\mathrm{sorted}}} f(x \setminus x_{\tau}) g(x_{\tau}),
    \end{equation*}
    and we conclude using the definition of the coefficient \( \mathsf{K}^{i+j}_i \).

label: lemma: sum over tau in Sjn with no braket along phi
title: Lemma
head: environment
labels: lemma: sum over tau in Sjn with no braket along phi
eqn: sum over tau in Sjn with no braket along phi

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is divided into two steps: the first one consists in showing that the set \( \{\tau \in S^{2q}_N : \tau\,\mathrm{sorted} \} \) over which the sum on the left-hand side is performed can be replaced by \( \{\tau \in S^{2q}_{\mathcal{T}^C} : \tau\,\mathrm{sorted,\,valid}\}\).
    The second step consists in showing that the brakets along variables indexed by \( \mathcal{T} = \left[m+1:N-2p\right] \setminus \{\ell_1, \ell_2\} \) are all equal to one.

    The first step relies on the fact that there are many permutations \( \tau \) such that the summand is necessarily zero due to the orthogonality \( \left\langle \begin{gathered} \varphi(y) \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} \chi_{2q}(y, \cdot) \end{gathered} \right\rangle_y = 0 \), and we can thus get rid of them.
    We are computing
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eqn: proof simplification sum over tau sorted - before doing anything}
        \sum_{\substack{\tau\in S^{2q}_N\\\tau\,\mathrm{sorted}}} \left\langle \begin{gathered} \varphi^{\otimes N-m-2p} \otimes \chi_{2p} \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} V_{\ell_1, \ell_2}\varphi^{\otimes N-2q}(x\setminus x_\tau) \chi_{2q}(x_\tau) \end{gathered} \right\rangle_{x_{\left[m+1:N\right]}},
    \end{equation}
     
    and the set \( \mathcal{T} \) is defined as the set of variables such that the left argument of the braket along each of these variables is \( \varphi \) and such that the operator \( V_{\ell_1, \ell_2} \) is not acting on them.
    If the permutation \( \tau \in S^{2q}_N \) is such that there is an index \( k \in \left[1:2q\right] \) for which \( \tau(k) \in \mathcal{T} \), then the braket along variable \( x_{\tau(k)} \) is \( \left\langle \begin{gathered} \varphi(y) \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} \chi_{2q}(y, \cdot \end{gathered} \right\rangle_y = 0 \) and the summand of \eqref{eqn: proof simplification sum over tau sorted - before doing anything} for that permutation vanishes.
    Therefore, the permutations \( \tau \in S^{2q}_N \) that don't necessarily give a vanishing summand are those for which \( \tau(\left[1:2q\right]) \subset \mathcal{T}^C := \left[1:m\right] \cup \{\ell_1, \ell_2\} \cup \left[N-2p+1:N\right] \), i.e. all \( \tau \in S^{2q}_{\mathcal{T}^C} \).
    We can argue similarly for brakets of the form \( \left\langle \begin{gathered} \chi_{2p}(y, \cdot) \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} \varphi(y) \end{gathered} \right\rangle_y = 0 \): they occur if a variable with index in \( \left[N-2p+1:N\right] \setminus \{\ell_1, \ell_2 \} \) corresponds to a function \( \varphi \) in the right argument of the braket, and this happens if \( \left[N-2p+1:N\right] \not\subset \tau \cup \{\ell_1, \ell_2\} \).
    Finally, the permutations we need to consider are the \emph{valid} (according to Definition \ref{def: valid permutation tau}) sorted permutations \( \tau\in S^{2q}_{\mathcal{T}^C} \).

    The second step of the proof is much shorter: for any such valid and sorted permutation \( \tau \), all the variables indexed by \( \mathcal{T} \) in \eqref{eqn: proof simplification sum over tau sorted - before doing anything} correspond to a braket \( \left\langle \begin{gathered} \varphi \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} \varphi \end{gathered} \right\rangle = 1 \).
    In other words, the multi-dimensional braket can be taken only on the variables \( \left[m+1:N\right] \setminus \mathcal{T} = (\{\ell_1, \ell_2\} \cup \left[N-2p+1:N\right]) \setminus \left[1:m\right] \), which is exactly the set \( \mathcal{B} \) defined in \eqref{eqn: def calB}.

label: lemma: operator splitting - potential hartree equation with phi0
title: Lemma
head: environment
labels: lemma: operator splitting - potential hartree equation with phi0
eqn: operator splitting - potential hartree equation with phi0

title: Proof
body_md:
For \( x \in \Omega \) and \( t\geq 0 \),
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\partial}{\partial t} |\varphi(t, x)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2
        &= \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \left( \overline{\varphi(t, x)} \varphi(t, x) \right)
            = \overline{\dot{\varphi}(t, x)} \varphi(t, x) + \overline{\varphi(t, x)} \dot{\varphi}(t, x)
            = 2 \mathrm{Re}\left( \overline{\varphi(t, x)} \dot{\varphi}(t, x) \right) \\
        &= 2 \mathrm{Re}\left( -\mathrm{i} \overline{\varphi(t, x)} (v \ast |\varphi(t)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2 - \mu_{\varphi(t)}) \varphi(t, x) \right) 
            = 2 \mathrm{Re}\left( -\mathrm{i} (v \ast |\varphi(t)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2 - \mu_{\varphi(t)}) |\varphi(t, x)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2 \right).
    \end{align*}
     
    The potential function \( v \) is a real function hence \( (v \ast |\varphi(t)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2 - \mu_{\varphi(t)}) |\varphi(t, x)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2 \) is real, and we get \( \frac{\partial}{\partial t} |\varphi(t, x)|\left.\vphantom{T_{j_0}^0}\!\!\right.^2 = 0 \).

label: lemma: associativity symmetric tensor product
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Associativity of symmetric tensor product
labels: lemma: associativity symmetric tensor product

title: Proof
body_md:
We have
    \begin{align*}
        ((f \otimes_s g) \otimes_s h)(x)
        &= \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}^{k+i+j}_k} \sum_{\tau\in S_{i+j+k}} (f\otimes_s g)(x_{\tau(\left[k+1:i+j+k\right])}) h(x_{\tau(\left[1:k\right])}) \\
        &= \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}^{k+i+j}_k \mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \sum_{\tau\in S_{i+j+k}} \sum_{\sigma \in S_{\tau(\left[k+1:i+j+k\right])}} f(x_{\sigma(\left[1:i\right])}) g(x_{\sigma(\left[i+1:i+j\right])}) h(x_{\tau(\left[1:k\right])}) \\
        &= \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}^{k+i+j}_k \mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \sum_{\tau_1 \in S_{i+j+k}^k} \sum_{\tau_2 \in S_{i+j+k \setminus \tau_1}} \sum_{\sigma \in S_{\tau_2}} f(x_{\sigma(\left[1:i\right])}) g(x_{\sigma(\left[i+1:i+j\right])}) h(x_{\tau_1}) \\
        &= \frac{(i+j)!}{\mathsf{K}^{k+i+j}_k \mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \sum_{\tau_1 \in S_{i+j+k}^k} \sum_{\sigma \in S_{i+j+k \setminus \tau_1}} f(x_{\sigma(\left[1:i\right])}) g(x_{\sigma(\left[i+1:i+j\right])}) h(x_{\tau_1}) \\
        &= \frac{(i+j)!}{\mathsf{K}^{k+i+j}_k \mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \sum_{\tau \in S_{i+j+k}} f(x_{\tau(\left[k+1:k+i\right])}) g(x_{\tau(\left[k+i+1:k+i+j\right])}) h(x_{\tau(\left[1:k\right])}).
    \end{align*}
     
    Similarly, 
    \begin{equation*}
        (f\otimes_s (g\otimes_s h))(x)
        = \frac{(j+k)!}{\mathsf{K}_i^{i+j+k} \mathsf{K}^{j+k}_j} \sum_{\tau \in S_{i+j+k}} f(x_{\tau(\left[k+1:k+i\right])}) g(x_{\tau(\left[k+i+1:k+i+j\right])}) h(x_{\tau(\left[1:k\right])}).
    \end{equation*}
     
    Thus,
    \begin{align*}
        ((f \otimes_s g) \otimes_s h)(x)
        &= \frac{(i+j)!}{\mathsf{K}^{k+i+j}_k \mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \frac{\mathsf{K}_i^{i+j+k} \mathsf{K}^{j+k}_j}{(j+k)!} (f\otimes_s (g\otimes_s h))(x) \\
        &= \frac{(i+j)!}{\sqrt{(i+j+k)!(i+j)!k! (i+j)!i!j!}} \frac{\sqrt{(i+j+k)!(j+k)!i! (j+k)!j!k!}}{(j+k)!} (f\otimes_s (g\otimes_s h))(x) \\
        &= (f\otimes_s (g\otimes_s h))(x).
    \end{align*}

    \begin{align*}

        &= \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \sum_{\sigma\in S_{i+j}} \left\langle \begin{gathered} f(x_{\sigma(\left[1:i\right])}) g(x_{\sigma(\left[i+1:i+j\right])}) \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} h(x) \end{gathered} \right\rangle 
            = \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}^{i+j}_j} \sum_{\sigma\in S_{i+j}} \left\langle \begin{gathered} f \otimes g \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} h \end{gathered} \right\rangle
            = \sqrt{\binom{i+j}{j}} \left\langle \begin{gathered} f \otimes g \end{gathered} \,\middle|\, \begin{gathered} h \end{gathered} \right\rangle.
    \end{align*}
